text:
jasmin: Heads-up — onboarding hit a confusing TS/edge mismatch. Sample works in local node (CJS) but types evaporate after bundling for the edge.

otto: ugh, more of the overload/generic collapse? can you paste the tiniest repro + env?

jasmin: yep. tiny repro attached inline:
```ts
// libs/wrappers.ts (sample)
export function callModel<T>(opts: { model: string }): Promise<T>;
export function callModel(opts: { model: string }){ return sdk.request(opts) }
// usage in quickstart.ts
const me = await callModel<{id: string, email: string}>({ model: 'ggml-mini' })
```
Locally me has correct type. After the edge bundle (we use Vite->Rollup, target = edge worker) `me` becomes `any`.

riyad: what's package.json + tsconfig for the sample? edge bundlers + the TS declaration pipeline can rewrite imports badly.

jasmin: package.json: `"type":"module"`, exports map is dual: `{"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs","types":"./dist/types/index.d.ts"}`. tsconfig: `{"target":"ES2022","module":"ES2020","moduleResolution":"bundler","declaration":true,"emitDeclarationOnly":false}`. We also run `dts-bundle-generator` in the edge build.

kelly: suspect #1: bundler/dts tooling flattened multiple .d.ts into a single surface and accidentally lost overload ordering (TS picks the first matching signature). suspect #2: the SDK shippped a conditional `export =` fallback which confuses declaration emit in NodeNext/ESM mixes.

otto: also check whether the edge build uses `tsserver` or `tsc` for checks — Vite sometimes uses esbuild for transpile-only and then a separate d.ts pipeline runs. If the dts tool re-exports as `declare const sdk: any; export = sdk;` inference will be gone.

jasmin: confirmed — the generated bundle.d.ts contains a local alias and ends with `export = sdk;` as a fallback. That appears to erase the generic overloads.

riyad: workaround options: A) avoid overloads in wrapper code (use a single generic signature or discriminated union), B) force the sample to use `moduleResolution: "node"` and point `types` explicitly at the ESM dts entry so bundler doesn't flatten, C) stop using `export =` in SDK typings (breaking change but correct long-term).

kelly: short-term pragmatic fix for the quickstart: change sample wrapper to `export function callModel<T>(opts: { model: string, mode?: 'json' }): Promise<T>` — adds a discriminant so TS has a clear single signature. Also update sample tsconfig: set `moduleResolution: "node"` during bundling step, and configure `dts-bundle-generator` with `preserveModule` so it doesn't rewrite types to a single namespace.

jasmin: I tried that. Quickstart PR switches the wrapper to a single generic signature and pins `moduleResolution: node` in sample tsconfig; CI for the sample (runs Vite+rollup + `tsc --noEmit`) now passes.

otto: there's also an auth/retry wrinkle: our `withAuth` wrapper used overloads to support callback-style and promise-style APIs. In the edge bundle code path the callback overload gets selected and the promise generic is widened to `unknown`, so people start casting with `as any` in onboarding. We should avoid overloads on those wrappers too.

riyad: agreed. Action items: 1) update quickstart sample code to avoid overloads in wrappers (minimal API change), 2) add an "Edge bundler TS caveats" section in onboarding README describing `moduleResolution`, `types` mapping, and dts tooling pitfalls, 3) add a sample-level CI job that runs the real bundler + `tsc --noEmit` to catch rewrites, 4) open SDK issue to evaluate removing `export =` fallback or adding `types/edge.d.ts` in exports.

kelly: also propose adding a lint rule to samples forbidding `as any` and `// @ts-ignore` so onboarding can't paper over these bugs. Keep the rule disabled for internal infra code only.

ci-bot: sample-ci: node-cjs typecheck: OK at 2951231200. edge-bundle typecheck: failed on master at 2951231220; branch `devex/quickstart-edge-typing` shows green.

jasmin: PR ready, linked in the issue. Long-term, SDK typing consolidation needed: avoid dual typings that create ambiguous declaration merges across ESM/CJS; consider shipping a small `types/edge.d.ts` entry to provide a canonical ESM view for bundlers.

otto: one more note — when we changed the SDK to support NodeNext we added `types` for both `import` and `require` paths. That helped CJS users but increases the probability bundlers pick the wrong d.ts. If we add an explicit `types.edge` export or a `types` map keyed by environment it would reduce ambiguity.

riyad: agreed. I'll spin up an SDK issue to track typings consolidation and test matrix (Node/CJS, Node/ESM, Edge/Vite, Edge/Cloudflare).

jasmin: TL;DR: generics+overloads + dts-bundling + conditional `export =` => inference erosion in edge bundles. Temporary fixes in sample + CI + docs; long-term SDK typing cleanup tracked in issue. PR attached to the issue. :sparkles:
